purpose: Native framebuffer setter and paged texture reader ABI/layout source migration
interpretation: Both setter prologues preserve two pointer registers and both R8D/R9D DWORD inputs. Their low word/byte are interpreted as handle/flag; the typed hook must preserve all DWORD bits.

Current framebuffer table is renderer+0xc97698 rather than old +0xc97690. Texture registry is +0xbde178 rather than +0xbde170. Framebuffer records retain stride0x68, color count+0x32 and depth handle+0x10.
Context descriptor-pointer fields +0x10/+0x18, stored handle+0x20, flag+0x2c, command list+0x30 and texture state cache+0x14458 remain in the current setter/transition path.
Both native texture lookup paths use 0xb8-byte records, 4096 inline entries, root/page links at +0xb8000, byte extent at +0xb8008 and mode byte at +0xb8018. Resource pointer is record+0.

Current cleanup +0xe80e690 tests record+0x9b bit0x40 before bypassing its ordinary pointer retirement path. Current override +0xe815030 calls cleanup, sets that bit and stores its input at record+0. These routines are not invoked as an acquisition or lease API.

Only actual public barrier resource arguments may be cloned as COM references; native registry pointers are copied and compared, never invoked. These joins do not establish backing heap/fence or exclusive scene ownership.
